rounds.text: Thejo Engineering Ltd demonstrates robust operational efficiency and profitability that significantly outpaces sector benchmarks, evidenced by a superior return on capital employed of 19.53% compared to the sector benchmark of 12.91% [E10], alongside a strong return on equity of 15.48% [E9]. Growth metrics are equally compelling, highlighted by a notable compounded sales growth of 25% over the trailing twelve months [E17] and a quarterly operating margin expansion reaching 15% in September 2026, marking an increase over the prior year [E30]. Financial stability is underpinned by conservative capitalization, featuring a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.12x [E36] and comfortable short-term liquidity supported by a current ratio of 2.70x [E37]. Institutional confidence is actively building, demonstrated by domestic institutions increasing their holding to 3.44% from 0.72% [E42], foreign institutions rising to 0.84% from 0.00% [E41], and an overall positive institutional money flow signal [E43]. Furthermore, the rules-based screen scores the company at a solid 80 out of 100 with a BUY recommendation, driven by strong year-over-year sales and net profit increases [E58, E59, E61]. Conceded: [E44].

Thejo Engineering Ltd trades at an expensive valuation that is unsupported by its intrinsic value calculations, carrying a significant margin of safety deficit of -23.1% based on a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 1629 against its market price of Rs 2005 [E44, E45]. Furthermore, the current market price implies an aggressive 16.9% earnings growth rate, which surpasses the base case assumption of 14.0% [E46], while earnings growth is actively decelerating [E63]. Multiple valuation multiples command heavy premiums over sector benchmarks, including a P/E of 37.44x versus 21.26x [E6], a P/B of 5.63x versus 2.31x [E7], and an EV/EBITDA of 20.91x versus 12.25x [E11]. Operating profitability has also faced structural pressure, with TTM operating margins contracting to 14% from 18% three years prior [E29], alongside creeping borrowings rising to Rs 46 Cr in Sep 2026 from Rs 41 Cr a year earlier [E38]. Conceded: [E10, E12, E21].

While the bear points to a DCF intrinsic value deficit [E44, E45] and a reverse DCF expectation gap [E46], the rules-based screen explicitly counters this by scoring a strong 80 out of 100 with a BUY rating [E58]. The bear's concern regarding decelerating earnings growth [E63] is directly contradicted by robust short-term momentum, including trailing twelve-month profit growth of 17% [E21], recent quarterly profit growth of 29% YoY [E61], and an increasing quarterly operating margin trend over the last 4 quarters [E32]. Although valuation multiples carry premiums over sector benchmarks [E6, E7, E11], these are fully justified by superior return metrics, with ROCE standing at an elite 19.53% against a sector benchmark of 12.91% [E10] and ROE at 15.48% versus 11.27% [E9], alongside a stellar 10-year median ROE of 20% [E25]. Conceded: [E29, E38, E44, E45, E46].

Conceded: [E58], [E61]. The bull leans on a rules-based screen score of 80/100 and YoY profit spikes to dismiss valuation warnings [E58, E61], yet ignores that the reverse DCF proves today's price of Rs 2,005 requires an aggressive 16.9% earnings growth rate that outstrips the baseline 14.0% expectation [E46]. Furthermore, pointing to trailing 17% profit growth [E21] and short-term quarterly margin increases [E32] does not erase the fundamental margin erosion visible in the TTM operating margin falling to 14% from 18% three years prior [E29]. While the bull celebrates superior return metrics like ROCE and ROE [E10, E9], those strengths are already aggressively priced in at a P/E of 37.44x and a P/B of 5.63x that sit well above sector benchmarks of 21.26x and 2.31x [E6, E7]. The intrinsic value model squarely places the intrinsic worth at Rs 1,629 per share, creating a glaring -23.1% margin of safety that makes the current valuation indefensible regardless of near-term momentum [E44, E45]. Conceded: [E32].
